$comment: Every brand asset slot, drawn by scripts/brand/draw.js and written by `npm run brand` into brand/<brand>/ as <slot>.svg (committed) and the raster `format` names (png keeps transparency, jpg for opaque artwork; gitignored, regenerated). A slot with `grounds` ships one file per ground (paper, ground) and one with `forms` one file per form (rect where there is room, round where it is small), named <slot>-<key>. A `template` is drawn per use, not exported.

slots.use: Full-colour emblem: report covers, the site page header, the source of every derivative
Single-colour seal (one ink): stamps, print, overlays on photography
Simplified mark that reads at 16-32 px: favicon, video watermark, inline badges
Seal left of the parent line and ceremonial name: page headers, letterhead, end cards
Seal over the name: square placements, report covers, closing credits
Name only, no seal: running heads, footers, tight horizontal space
Blind-embossed seal for paper grounds: page backgrounds, certificates, end cards
ENTERED INTO THE PUBLIC RECORD: a published inquiry, the closing card (red ink)
FINDING: marks the answer section; never decoration (charter 2.2) (the brand's ground ink)
AMENDED: a dated correction (red ink)
UNDER EXAMINATION: a story not yet published (slate ink)
YouTube channel banner; masthead inside the central 1546x423 safe area
X / Twitter profile header
Site header band for the institution page
Share card for the brand's pages (og:image, twitter:image)

Share-card template for one inquiry: the question as text over the brand's ground, seal and full name below (drawn per story by `npm run brand` into public/og/stories/<topic>/<story slug>.jpg; not in the kit export)
Video to site: "Read the full record" (description header, end screen, posts)
Site to video: "Watch the inquiry"
YouTube end screen with slots for the subscribe element and two videos
Closing card: "The matter is now part of the public record."
Profile picture on every platform (YouTube, X, Bluesky); usually the seal on a clean ground
YouTube branding watermark; derived from mark-small, not the avatar scaled down
Small emblem in a thumbnail corner
